blocks.content: So far the shape only moves in one direction. In Brick Breaker the ball moves in two directions at once and bounces off every wall. That behavior comes from velocity.
Velocity is just two variables. dx for horizontal movement and dy for vertical movement. Each frame, dx gets added to x and dy gets added to y. That is all movement is.

Click Run Code and you will see the ball bouncing around all four walls.

Here, each frame x += dx and y += dy move the ball by its velocity. When the ball reaches a wall, flipping the sign of dx reverses horizontal direction. The same applies to dy for the top and bottom walls. That is the entire bouncing mechanic for Brick Breaker's ball.

Velocity is powerful because the sign encodes direction and the magnitude encodes speed - all in one number. To make the ball move faster, increase dx. To reverse direction, negate dx. You never need to track "which direction is it moving" separately. I think of dx and dy as the ball's intention - where it wants to go this frame - and the boundary checks as the game world's response.
